title: Failure & policy gates
blurb: Triggers six real Translator refusal paths without downloading a model — expired gesture (NotAllowedError), denied iframe permissions policy, invalid BCP 47 tag (RangeError), missing targetLanguage (TypeError), unsupported pair (NotSupportedError), and aborted signal (AbortError) — plus an inference check for TranslatorAPIAllowed=false.
question: Which exact exception types and availability values does Translator produce across missing user activation, Permissions Policy denial, invalid options, unsupported pairs, AbortSignal cancellation, and enterprise policy lockout?
result: On Chrome for Testing 153 headless (Linux), 6/6 refusal gates matched spec (NotAllowedError after 6 s gesture expiry, iframe allow="translator 'none'" returned unavailable + NotAllowedError, invalid tag threw RangeError, missing targetLanguage threw TypeError, en->kl threw NotSupportedError, pre-aborted signal threw AbortError), and the policy check reported not blocking. Managed Android TranslatorAPIAllowed=false not verified.
testedIn: Chrome for Testing 153 headless (Linux, 6/6 refusal gates verified); managed Android Chrome 161 TranslatorAPIAllowed=false not verified

friction.summary: Calling Translator.create() for a downloadable pair without transient user activation can take several seconds before rejecting with NotAllowedError
friction.repro: Wait 6 seconds after a click so transient activation expires, then call Translator.create({ sourceLanguage: 'en', targetLanguage: 'fr' }) on a downloadable pair; rejection was observed only after several seconds in headless Chrome 153.
friction.workaround: Gate create() behind a direct user tap whenever availability() is not "available", and wrap create() with an AbortController watchdog.
